content.content:
The detail panel's four relationship sections (rmovtvkt) list ids, and an id listed there that names no node document takes none of the cues that promise activation: no pointer cursor is shown over it, no underline is drawn under it while a pointer is over it, and no outline is drawn around it while it has focus. The case is exactly the one rusopkql settles — a dependency or evaluation the selected node declares whose other end names no node document — and the three cues are the whole of this decision. Each cue says that the entry will answer when it is clicked or focused, and on this entry nothing answers: activating it changes nothing at all (rusopkql). Withholding the cues is the smallest thing that stops the entry from making a promise the viewer will not keep, and it is the only thing this decision does: the entry is not presented as clickable, and nothing else about it is changed.

No pointer cursor is shown over the entry. A pointer that changes shape over an entry is what tells a reader, before anything is clicked, that the id is something to invoke; over this entry the pointer stays as it is, so passing over it promises nothing. Nothing is put in the pointer cue's place: the entry is not given a blocked, "not allowed" or otherwise bespoke cursor, because a cursor chosen to say "this one will not work" is a mark on the entry and this decision adds no mark. Which cursor the text around the entry shows is not settled here; this decision only withholds the pointer cue from the entry.

No underline is drawn under the entry when a pointer is over it. The hover underline is the cue that the pointer has arrived at something invocable, and there is nothing here to arrive at, so hovering adds nothing to the entry: it looks the same under the pointer as away from it. Nor does another hover mark stand in for the underline — no strikethrough, no dotted or dashed rule, no hover treatment that signals something else is wrong. The entry's appearance away from the pointer, and the colour role it takes at rest, on hover and on focus, are not decided here; this decision withdraws the hover underline and nothing more.

No outline is drawn around the entry while it has focus. The focus outline is the cue that says where the keyboard is standing and that the thing under it can be invoked; on an entry whose activation does nothing, drawing it would invite a keystroke and answer it with nothing, the same false promise in the keyboard's terms. The statement is about the drawn indicator only: whether focus lands on a listed entry, and what Enter or Space does when it does, are kwxutvpw's and stand exactly as recorded, so this decision removes no input, does not make the entry unclickable or unreachable, and does not change the inertness rusopkql settles. Nothing is substituted for the outline in the outline's role — no border, glow or second outline appears to say what the outline would have said — and whether the entry's colour role treats focus differently is not decided here.

None of this re-decides which entries are links. mwwxxzyk commits a listed id to reading as a visible link rather than bare text, and it expressly leaves the id that names no node document to the decisions that own that case, allowing it to be presented like its siblings or muted and without the link cue. This decision is one of those decisions and exercises that carve for exactly three cues: it says nothing against mwwxxzyk where an id names a node, exempts no other entry, and adds no exception to the four sections or to what they list (rmovtvkt). Nor does it say that this entry is not an entry, or that it reads as ordinary prose: the entry keeps its place among its siblings, its text stays the bare id, and how far a listed id that names no node still reads as a link is left to the colour role and the stylesheet decisions that own the rest of its look. Nothing here states that an entry naming a node does show these three cues either; whether it does is settled where each cue is owned, and this decision withholds them only from the entry that cannot follow its id to a node.

The abstention is not a mark. rusopkql keeps the entry listed among its siblings and inert when activated, carrying no mark of its own, and its wording about the entry's plain look adds no appearance while handing styling and any focus indicator to the presentation decisions; this decision adds nothing to that account and narrows no outcome rusopkql fixes. No warning glyph, placeholder or stand-in text, "missing" label, icon, strikethrough or annotation says anything about the node document here; nothing is hidden, dropped, filtered out or replaced; and nothing presents the entry as a disabled control, no disabled styling and no unavailable-state treatment standing in for the three cues. The panel and the canvas keep one account of a recorded condition: the edge stays marked where it is drawn (tqxvykwn) and stays listed, plain and inert, where the node's relationships are reported (rusopkql). The colour role the entry takes, muted or otherwise, is not decided here.

Behaviour is untouched. A pointer click, or Enter or Space while the entry has focus, still changes nothing (rusopkql): the selection and the detail panel stay as they were, and no input is added or removed. What is settled is the entry's own presentation of three cues — not what activating the entry does, not what the canvas draws for the unresolved edge (tqxvykwn), not whether a node document is opened, and not where focus moves after the entry. No class, style property or stylesheet rule is named: which element carries the pointer, hover and focus cues for an entry that names a node, and the class vocabulary that would distinguish this entry from its siblings, belong to the decisions that build the surface and write the styles.
content.rationale:
kwxutvpw made every listed id an activatable entry and mwwxxzyk made a listed id read as a link, and each left one case open: the id that names no node document. rusopkql settled that case's behaviour — the entry stays listed and activating it changes nothing — and handed its appearance to the presentation decisions, exactly as mwwxxzyk left the look of the case open. What remained was the gap between the two: an entry dressed in the cues that say "invoke me", on which nothing happens when it is invoked. Withdrawing those cues is the smallest honest answer to that gap, because it costs no element, no text, no behaviour and no new rule, and because a reader who is not promised an outcome cannot be disappointed by it.

The three cues are the panel's activation vocabulary at the level of the entry's own state — a pointer cursor says the pointer is over something that responds, a hover underline says the pointer has reached something invocable, a focus outline says the keyboard is standing on a control that will act — and each is a promise this entry cannot keep. Withdrawing all three is the minimum that removes the promise; withdrawing fewer leaves one of them making it, and the reader who follows the remaining cue has been told the same untrue thing, more quietly. Withdrawing more would exceed the case: a blocked cursor, a warning glyph, a strikethrough or a placeholder would be a mark, and rusopkql's entry carries no mark of its own, because the mark that condition needs is the canvas's (tqxvykwn), drawn where the edge is. So the abstention stops at the cues and never becomes a statement that the entry, its node or its edge is missing, broken or disabled.

Each alternative was a different commitment or a contradiction. Hiding, dropping or filtering out the entry would make the panel stop reporting an edge the node records, which rusopkql forbids and which would set the panel against the canvas's mark. Presenting the entry as disabled or unavailable would make an ordinary recorded state — the graph referencing an id no document carries, which tqxvykwn already shows as an unresolved edge — look like a viewer fault, the same error rusopkql refuses for activation. And declaring the entry not a link would reverse mwwxxzyk for a case mwwxxzyk deliberately handed over, when the link look of an entry that names no node is not this decision's to settle beyond the cues it withdraws.

That is why the decision is this narrow. The colour role the entry takes, muted or otherwise, at rest, on hover and on focus, is a separate commitment with its own check; the class vocabulary, the element that carries each cue and the stylesheet rules that draw them belong to the surface and the styles; the activation the entry does not perform, the canvas marking, opening a document and where focus moves next are each already owned or out of scope. Settled here, any of them would be restated or contradicted by the decision that owns it, and the distinction that matters to the reader — an entry that cannot be followed, as against an entry that is broken — would be lost.

The cost is real and is accepted deliberately. Focus can still land on the entry, as kwxutvpw leaves it, and the entry now answers nothing there and is not drawn as the place the keyboard stands; an indicator is given up so that no control is offered where none acts. Reachability, inertness, the id the entry shows and the one account the panel and the canvas give of the recorded condition all remain what their own decisions made them, and with the cues gone the reader who reaches the entry learns from it what the viewer actually does: nothing.
